messages:
lina: Hey team — first day! Trying to follow the k8s onboarding doc but I can’t talk to the cluster from my laptop. `kubectl get pods -n team-data` returns an error:
```
Unable to connect to the server: dial tcp 10.12.34.56:6443: i/o timeout
```
Can someone point me at the right kubeconfig/context and who to ask for namespace access? TIA :wave:

devon: welcome aboard, lina! Quick checklist: 1) confirm your kubeconfig is the one from `~/.kube/config` we provisioned; 2) check current context: `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts -o name`. Typical output we expect:
```
$ kubectl config current-context
redwood-dev@redwood-cluster
$ kubectl config get-contexts -o name
redwood-dev@redwood-cluster
redwood-prod@redwood-cluster
```
If your context is wrong, `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev@redwood-cluster`. Also run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-data` to see if you already have RBAC. If you don’t, open the access form here: https://redwood.internal/access-requests and put `team-data` as the namespace and `k8s:developer` as the role. If you prefer I can file it for you.

lina: ran the checks — current-context is `redwood-dev@redwood-cluster` but `can-i` says no: 
```
$ kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-data
no
```
I filed the access form but it asked for manager approval, which might take a bit.

infra-bot: Access request #AK-12897 created for user lina. Approver: @maria. Status: pending. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/AK-12897

maria: Hi @lina — I can expedite. Please DM me your GitHub handle (we use that to map to AD group). I’ll add you to `team-data-devs` which grants `view` and `list` for the namespace; if you need `edit` say so. Also confirm you completed SSO setup so your identity syncs.

lina: thanks! my github handle is linacodes. SSO is set up (okta).

maria: Got it, filing an admin bind now. I'll post when complete.

samuel: FYI once you have the permissions, you can make a local context with the namespace baked in: 
```
kubectl config set-context default-team-data --namespace=team-data --cluster=redwood-dev@redwood-cluster --user=linacodes
kubectl config use-context default-team-data
```
That way `kubectl get pods` will hit team-data by default. Also note: avoid running broad `kubectl delete` commands unless paired with `--dry-run=client` first. If you need to port-forward a service for local dev: `kubectl -n team-data port-forward svc/metrics-exporter 9090:80` (but watch local ports). Ping me if anything still times out. :thumbsup:

maria: Access granted and AD group updated — you should be able to `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-data` now.

lina: confirmed! `yes` now. Thank you all, really appreciate the fast help :sparkles:
